Ukraine yarakoze n'ibindi bitero muri Afrika, aho ingabo zayo zateye abarwanyi b'abacangero b'Uburusiya bo mu murwi wa Africa Corps, wasubiriye umurwi Wagner wagirizwa kuhonyanga uburenganzira bwa muntu incuro nyinshi.

Si Uburusiya bwonyene butewe ubwoba n'iki gitero ca vuba ku kivuko ca Benghazi. Ubutumwa bwa ONU muri Libya na bwo nyene bwagaragaje "impungenge zikomeye".

Abategetsi ba Libya bavuga ko igihugu cabo kitari mu ntambara iri hagati y'Uburusiya na Ukraine, naho ubwato Merkury hamwe n'ubundi bwato bwari butwaye imizigo bwatewe mu buseruko bwa Libya, agace kagenzurwa na Khalifa Haftar, uyu akaba ari intwazangabo isanzwe ari somambike n'Uburusiya.

Muri uno mwaka, Ishirahamwe Mpuzamakungu rishinzwe uruja n'uruza rwo mu mazi (IMO) ntiryahengeshanije kwiyamiriza ibitero vyose vyagabwa ku mato y'ubudandaji aca mu Muhora wa Hormuz, abakora mu bijanye kwunguruza ibintu mu mazi kw'isi yose bakaba bibaza nimba ico gitero kitoba kigiye gutanga akarorero kabi gashobora gutuma n'ahandi hagabwa ibitero nk'ivyo ku mato y'ubudandaji.

Nimba Ukraine ishobora gutegura no gushira mu ngiro igitero nk'iki ku mato y'Uburusiya ari ku kivuko gifatwa nk'ikitagira uruhande cegamiye kandi kiri kure cane, ikibazo ni iki: ivyo bizogarukira hehe?

Mu gihe hasigaye igihe gito ngo imyaka itanu ihere kuva Uburusiya butanguye intambara yabwo yeruye kuri Ukraine, iza yamaze gukwira no mu bindi bice vy'Uburayi.

Ku wa gatanu, ibisasu vyinshi vy'Uburusiya vyaguye muri Pologne, hirya cane nko ku bilometero 100 gusa uvuye ahabera imyimenyerezo rusangi y'ingabo z'Ubwongereza n'iz'Ubufaransa zitegurwa kuzorungikwa muri Ukraine mu gihe hoba amasezerano yo guhagarika intambara.

Umushikiranganji wa mbere wa Pologne Donald Tusk yavuze ko ako ari "agasotoro" kakozwe n'Uburusiya n'ibigirankana.

Si ubwa mbere ibisasu vy'Uburusiya biguye muri Pologne, ni ukuvuga mu karere ka OTAN, abakurikiranira hagufi ibintu bakavuga ko Uburusiya buriko buvogera n'ibigirankana imbibe za OTAN kugira ngo burabe ingene ivyifatamwo, bamwe bagasaba ko ifata ingingo ruhasha.

Ariko rero Uburusiya bumaze gufatirwa ibihano vyinshi n'ibihugu vy'Uburengero, aho Uburaya bumaze kugabanya igice kinini c'igitoro na gaze bwakura mu Burusiya, naho butabihagaritse vyose. Rero bituma inzira zo kwihora ivyo bihugu vyofata ziba nke cane, kiretse kwinjira mu ntambara, ivyo ata gihugu na kimwe gishaka.

Ibihugu vya Romania na Moldavie na vyo vyisanga biriko biraterwa n'amadrone y'Uburusiya avogera ikirere cavyo aja gutera ibivuko vya Ukraine ku Kiyaga Cirabura, mu gihe amato y'ubudandaji ya Bulgaria na Romania na yo yagiye aterwa n'amadrone yo mu mazi hafi y'inkengera zavyo mu Kiyaga Cirabura.

Muri Romania, umunywanyi wa OTAN, vyabaye ngombwa ko indege z'intambara zirungikwa mu bubangutsi kugira ngo zizibire amadrone y'Uburusiya avogera ikirere cayo, kandi atari mu buryo bw'impanuka, ahubwo ko bwayarungika n'ibigirankana.

Ibihugu bitatu vya Baltique, ari vyo Estonia, Lettonie na Lituanie, vyose bisangiye imbibe n'Uburusiya kandi vyose vyifata ko biri ku murongo w'imbere muri iyi ntambara.

Hagiye haba ibitero bitamenyekanye amamuko yavyo ku nganda za gisirikare muri ivyo bihugu, bigashirwa ku gatwe k'abantu bakorera Uburusiya.

Ku ruhande rwabwo, Uburusiya bwikeka ko Estonia ifasha Ukraine mu bitero vy'amadrone ku karere ka Baltique aciye mu kirere ca Estonia.

Intambara y'uruvangatirane si ikintu gishasha, ariko iriko yiyongera.

Iyi iba mu gihe uruhande rumwe rukoresha uburyo rwihishwa kandi bugoye kumenya neza uwuri inyuma yayo, nko mu gukora ibitero vyo kuri internet, guturira ibibanza bibikwamwo ibikoresho vya gisirikare, canke gukoresha amadrone, yaba aya maneko canke yikoreye ibiturika.

Mu gihe c'iremba giheze, ikibuga c'indege ca Leipzig-Halle mu Budagi, gikoreshwa mu gupakira imizigo ija muri Ukraine, caratewe n'amadrone atatu yari yikoreye ibiturika, ariko akaba yabonywe imbere y'uko akora ibara.

Hari n'ibindi vyabaye hirya no hino ku mugabane wa Buraya, aho ibiboho vyari vyikoreye ibiturika vyarungitswe mu bihugu bitandukanye, cane cane mu Budagi, muri Pologne no mu Bwongereza. Uburusiya burahakana uruhara rwabwo,

MN202611_14lrb6gj8l2.t:
Carla Ward has been in charge of the Republic of Ireland since 2025

Republic of Ireland manager Carla Ward has signed a contract extension until the conclusion of the side's Euro 2029 campaign.

The 42-year-old's previous deal was due to expire at the end of this World Cup qualification cycle but her future has now been resolved before next month's two-legged play-off final against Poland.

Ward replaced Eileen Gleeson at the helm in January 2025 and has led the side to promotion to League A in the Nations League and a highest ever position of 21st in the Fifa rankings.

The Republic of Ireland are just 180 minutes from next summer's World Cup in Brazil, with the first leg against Poland in Gdansk on 1 December before the reverse fixture four days later at Aviva Stadium.

"From the moment I arrived, I've felt a strong connection with this country, the players, the staff and, most importantly, the people. The way I've been welcomed and embraced has meant a huge amount to me, and it's a real privilege to lead this team and this nation," said Ward.

"I'm incredibly proud of what we've achieved together so far, but what excites me most is what lies ahead. There's something really special about this group, their togetherness, their character and their willingness to fight for each other and for the jersey.

"I've always said I want to build something that people can connect with, a team that reflects the spirit of this country, that people are proud of and genuinely feel part of. We've had some brilliant moments already, but I really believe we're only just getting started."

Two down, two to go - Irish target back-to-back World Cups

Mustaki out of World Cup play-off with knee injury

Ward previously managed Sheffield United, Aston Villa and Birmingham City after a successful playing career during which she scored over 100 goals for Sheffield FC.

Since she became boss, the Republic of Ireland have won 12 of their 19 games and lost just one of their Nations League fixtures last year with the sole reverse coming away to Slovenia.

Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive officer David Courell said Ward has helped give "women and girls' football around the country the platform it deserves" during her tenure.

"We are delighted to reach agreement with Carla to continue to lead our Ireland women's national team for the long term," he added.

"The energy that she has brought to the role has propelled the team towards, hopefully, qualifying for a second Fifa Women's World Cup and, in turn, giving women and girls' football around the country the platform it deserves.

"Extending Carla's contract shows our ambition to keep moving forward, hopefully to the World Cup in Brazil and beyond to the Uefa European Championships in Germany in 2029."

The Republic of Ireland are aiming to secure a spot at their second successive World Cup, while Poland have never qualified for the tournament before.

Ward's side defeated Kazakhstan in comfortable fashion in their play-off semi-final with Poland coming through a penalty shootout against Belgium.

Republic of Ireland must do without key defender Chloe Mustaki who has been forced to withdraw from the panel after rupturing her anterior cruciate ligament (ACL).

Duncan Ferguson jointly holds the record for the most red cards in Premier League history with eight.

Glentoran manager Duncan Ferguson has been suspended for seven games following his red card in the side's 3-2 defeat by Cliftonville last week.

The former Everton striker was dismissed for how he addressed match officials after believing the Reds' opener at Solitude should have been ruled out for a foul in the build-up.

The 1995 FA Cup winner arrived at the Oval in October and has so far won one, drawn two and lost one of his four games in charge.

"I want to apologise to the match officials for my behaviour on Friday night," said the former Forest Green Rovers and Inverness Caledonian Thistle boss.

"I was frustrated by what happened on the pitch and let my emotions get the better of me. I went too far in the way I expressed that frustration towards the officials, and I should have handled the situation better."

"I accept the suspension and I'll learn from what happened. My focus now is on the players, the staff and the work we've got to do together, both on and off the pitch."

The sanction will start with Tuesday night's hosting of Larne in the Bet McLean Cup, a competition in which the east Belfast outfit have been beaten finalists the past two seasons.

Even should the Glens progress to the quarter-finals of the competition expected to take place next month, Ferguson's ban would still include the eagerly anticipated Boxing Day visit from fierce rivals Linfield.

Cav Miley has made 17 appearances since joining Chelmsford in the summer

Footballers may be among the fittest athletes in the world of sport, but they are not immune to bizarre injuries.

Dave Beasant famously severed a tendon in his big toe when he dropped a bottle of salad cream, while Rio Ferdinand strained tendons in his knee by lying in one position on the sofa for too long watching television.

The latest inductee into the strange injury hall of fame is Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley.

The 31-year-old midfielder missed the 2-2 draw with Walton and Hersham in the National League South on Saturday after twisting an ankle in training by falling down a badger hole.

Miley returned for the 1-0 home victory over Maidstone United on Monday, after which manager Mark Cooper shed more light on the incident.

"Everyone is telling me it's gone viral, but I told the truth - he fell down a badger hole," Cooper told the club's YouTube channel.

"I was told at the start it was a fox hole, but then the guy at where we train told me it's a badger hole.

"We need to make sure we fill all of them in before we train now."

Miley joined Chelmsford in the summer after spells in the National League with Southend United and Eastleigh.

Scottish striker Kirsty Howat signed for Crystal Palace in September 2025

Crystal Palace have been deducted three points after using too many substitution windows during their win on the opening day of the 2026-27 Women's Super League season.

Palace, who were playing their first match following promotion back to the WSL, beat Everton 1-0 on 6 September at Gander Green Lane.

However, manager Jo Potter brought on Kirsty Howat for Shannon O'Brien in the seventh minute of second-half stoppage time to try and shore up the victory.

It was the fourth separate substitution made by Potter, who had also made changes in the 62nd, 83rd and 90th minutes.

While WSL managers are allowed to make five changes in a game, they must be made across only three stoppages in play to avoid excessive time wasting.

Palace have been stripped of the three points they earned in the match - one of only two WSL games the Eagles have won this season.

This punishment drops Palace down one place in the WSL table to 13th - the relegation play-off place.

Palace are now below fellow promoted side Birmingham City in the table on goal difference, with both sides now having six points - six behind Everton in 11th.

In a statement on their club website , external Palace said they were "disappointed" by the decision.

The decision was made by an independent tribunal after Palace admitted the breach of competition rule 5.19.1.

The rule states: "A substitution can only be made when play is stopped for any reason and the referee has given permission. A club at its discretion may use five substitute players during a match. For the avoidance of doubt, each club has no more than three substitution opportunities in each match."

The tribunal said that while the rule breach was inadvertent and "not intended to secure an unfair advantage", it said a points deduction was necessary in order to provide a deterrent to clubs against making a similar mistake in future.

"The integrity of the competition would be damaged if a club that had breached the rules on substitution opportunities, and had won the match, were allowed to keep the points it obtained, save in exceptional circumstances," the tribunal stated in its full written decision. , external

They said the lateness of the substitution in the match - so late that Howat did not touch the ball after coming on - did not excuse Palace from punishment.

It also ruled "that responsibility for complying with the rule rests with clubs, not match officials".

Palace - who placed the word "fourth" in inverted commas in their response to the ruling - are aiming to improve on their only previous WSL campaign in 2024-25, where they only won twice in 22 matches and were relegated by a 10-point margin.

Their statement read: "Everyone at the club is obviously frustrated that such a minor infraction, given that the player was on the pitch for only 46 seconds while the ball was in play, has led to such a significant penalty – a penalty which we do not agree is reasonable or proportionate.

"We are disappointed for the players and staff who worked so hard to secure a deserved victory on our return to the WSL."

Forward Lexi Lloyd-Smith had scored the only goal of the game in the 34th minute on her Palace debut.

Between 2013 and 2026, almost 250,000 badgers were killed in England as part of widespread culling to tackle bovine tuberculosis (TB)

Plaid Cymru ministers have ruled out a mass badger cull as part of updated plans to tackle bovine tuberculosis (TB).

It follows months of speculation over the Welsh government's intentions, after an expert group warned "a step change" was needed in efforts to eradicate the disease.

While farming leaders have long called for tougher badger controls, a petition against culling has attracted more than 28,000 signatures on the Senedd website in recent weeks.

The Welsh government said it would take "a new and pragmatic approach to TB eradication that is evidence-based and science-led".

Reform calls for badger cull in fight against bovine TB

Young farmer in tears after TB hits 55 cows

Latest figures show nearly 96% of cattle herds in Wales are now TB free.

But the problem - which can be devastating for affected farms - is concentrated, with higher incidence levels in west Wales and along the border with England.

There were 10,090 cows slaughtered following TB testing in the 12 months to June 2026.

Under the previous Labour-run Welsh government, a target was set for Wales to completely eradicate bovine TB by 2041.

But before May's Senedd election an expert group set up to advise ministers , external warned that goal would "not be met", and called for urgent action and more funding.

Cattle are slaughtered if they are found to be carriers of bovine TB

The Bovine TB Eradication Programme Board's latest recommendations were published on Tuesday, alongside the government's response.

On badgers, ministers said they were "not pursuing a mass, non-selective cull".

However further research is proposed of the role played by badgers and deer in spreading the disease via new population surveys and fieldwork.

This would then lead to developing "targeted and proportionate" interventions which could include trapping and testing badgers before vaccinating or euthanising them, "where the evidence supports this".

Localised trapping and culling was trialled in Wales on nine farms between 2017 and 2024, but the cost involved drew criticism after hundreds of thousands of pounds was spent on killing a small number of badgers.

Officials told a briefing for journalists that "selective removal" of badgers was a possibility in future, but "[we] cannot give you a timeline".

In July, the Senedd backed a Reform UK motion calling on the Welsh Government to consider targeted wildlife control, including badger culling

Changes to cattle testing were also being proposed by the government, to help spot infection earlier.

They will work with the farming industry to explore "safe ways" of moving cattle out of TB restricted herds, to help businesses continue to operate.

Farms experiencing persistent issues and under so-called enhanced management will be offered more choice in how their situation is handled.

There is talk of a new advisory service for farmers and vets - and moves to provide better, more up-to-date data on the latest disease risk.

For farming families "a TB breakdown can mean months or years of restrictions, uncertainty and difficult choices", said agriculture minister Llyr Gruffydd

Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability, Llyr Gruffydd MS, said bovine TB remained "one of the most serious animal health challenges facing Wales".

"We will not stand by while farmers face uncertainty and anxiety, nor will we pursue a mass non-selective cull," he added.

"Instead, we will be taking evidence-based and science-led action, incorporating the three pillars of cattle, people and wildlife.

"Farmers and the public will rightly judge us on whether we prevent disease and reduce its impact, even when the decisions are difficult."

Ian Rickman, president of Farmers' Union of Wales, said it was "positive to note that targeted and proportionate action will now be taken on TB in wildlife where evidence supports this approach".

"With the loss of over 92,000 cattle and the percentage of herds under Bovine TB having remained stubbornly consistent for the past ten years, this is now the opportunity to intensify the co-working between industry, the veterinary profession, academics and government in order to deliver these recommendations without delay and further explore the wider proposals set out by the Programme Board," he added.

MN202611_22go08dmg6.t:
The explosion ripped through one of the city's central squares

A car bomb has exploded in the central Colombian city of Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.

The explosive device was detonated in front of the offices of the regional government, in the city centre, damaging several buildings.

No group has so far admitted carrying out the attack - the latest in a series using explosives to target official buildings and security forces' headquarters.

Colombian President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed "narcoterrorism", but gave no details. Armed criminal groups have recently stepped up attacks in what appears to be retaliation for an offensive ordered against them by De la Espriella.

Writing on social media, the president said that his government would "bluntly and forcefully" respond , external to "every drop of Colombian blood spilled".

"There will be no impunity and no retreat," he added.

It is the latest in a series of attacks targeting official buildings and security forces' headquarters

Three weeks ago, three adults and a baby were killed in a car bomb attack near army barracks in Tolima province .

And earlier on Monday, drones dropped explosives on the police headquarters in the northern city of Cúcuta.

The car bomb in Villavicencio went off on Monday evening - the eve of the 10th anniversary of the signing of a peace deal between the government and left-wing rebels of the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (Farc), Colombia's largest guerrilla group.

Following the signing of the deal, thousands of left-wing rebel fighters laid down their arms.

However, a significant number of Farc members, who did not agree with the deal, refused to disarm and joined dissident groups instead.

While forced displacement, child recruitment and the numbers of attacks on security forces dropped in the aftermath of the deal, there has been an upsurge in recent years driven by dissident Farc factions and criminal groups fighting for control of drug trafficking, illegal mining and extortion rackets.

Colombia's first left-wing president, who was in power from August 2022 to August 2026, tried to negotiate with these armed groups as part of what he called his "total peace" strategy.

However, the talks stalled and collapsed with several of the criminal groups violating ceasefires they had agreed to observe.

De la Espriella was elected on a promise to crack down on "narcoterrorism" and has been scathing about his predecessor's approach.

He has also been critical of the 2016 agreement, calling it a "false peace".

In a post on X, uploaded shortly before news of the car bomb in Villavicencio spread, he referred to the peace deal as a "mess", describing it as a "waste of public resources" and the "cause behind Colombia's ruin".

Former President Juan Manuel Santos and Rodrigo Londoño - the two men who signed the peace deal on behalf of the Colombian government and the Farc respectively - defended it in an interview with BBC Mundo ahead of the anniversary .

Santos said that De la Espriella was "totally wrong" to call it a "false peace".

"He wants to use, or has bought into that cynical and mistaken theory that the violence we see today is the result of the peace deal, when the exact opposite is the case," Santos said, arguing that the problem lies with the lack of implementation of the agreement.

Pope Francis claimed he saw the devil three times over the course of his life, as well as the "gates of hell", according to new extracts from his private diary.

In The Private Diary of Pope Francis, published on Tuesday, a 2021 entry lists the late pontiff as having three visions of the devil: once from a car, another "in the choir loft" during Mass, and a third during a meeting with Vatican officials.

"I can't forget the powerful raspiness of his voice," Francis wrote, recalling one of the visions.

In the diary, written from 1992 to 2024, he also expresses regret over his 2018 visit to Chile, when he was criticised for defending a bishop who was accused of covering up sexual abuse committed by a priest.

Francis, who led the Catholic Church for 12 years until his death in 2025, later apologised and summoned the country's bishops to Rome, where they all offered to resign .

"Devastated because of the situation in Chile," Francis wrote in a 2021 entry.

"It was hard for me to admit what happened in Chile; I didn't think it was so serious."

Of his encounters, which Francis interpreted as meetings with the devil, he said he could not forget the devil's "menacing" eyes.

"He looked at me with flaming eyes... more intense than the previous one. They were like flashes of fire," he wrote of his second vision that he said happened inside a Carmelite chapel while he was archbishop of Buenos Aires.

He said the devil's presence intruded on his journeys, including during the visit to Chile amid the clerical sexual abuse scandal, and a meeting a few days after he had returned to Rome.

"I saw him and heard his voice, triumphant, possessing everything," he wrote, adding that "the Lord gave me the chance to free myself from these encounters".

The collection of diaries was edited by a longtime friend of Francis

The late pope also revealed that while getting ready to go to sleep in June 2018, he "saw the gates of hell".

"I watched a little, and it terrified me," he said, adding that he "took the rosary as a weapon".

"It's dangerous to get close to the gates of hell, because flames can spring out and burn," he wrote.

Cardinal Victor Fernandez, head of the Vatican's Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith and friend of Francis, edited the diaries, which are the first by a pope to be released to the public since the 1960s.

Pope Francis was elected pope in 2013 and died aged 88 in April 2025.

Senegal are the rightful Champions of Africa Cup of Nations 2025 and not Morocco, the Court of Arbitration for Sports has overruled.

Prof. Ulrich Haas, the President of the Court of Arbitration for Sports Panel in Lausanne, Switzerland announced the ruling on Tuesday.

The ruling brings an end to the controversies surrounding the AFCON final match between Senegal and Morocco.

The two countries had taken their dispute to the Confederation of African Football, (CAF) for handling. CAF decided that Morroco had won the game.

“Having considered all the submissions, evidence and applicable regulations, the Panel finds that the decision of CAF was affected by procedural irregularities and a breach of the principles of natural justice and that the result of the final match played on 18th January, 2026 must be upheld,” reads the ruling in part.

Senegal defeated hosts Morocco 1–0 in extra time at the Prince Moulay Abdellah Stadium in Rabat in which players and head coach Pape Thiaw walked off the pitch for 15 minutes over a late penalty call against Senegal, amid wider crowd trouble. Morocco missed the penalty.

“CAF is instructed to implement this award immediately and to make the necessary adjustments to the official records, including the trophy, medal distribution and rankings,” rules CAS.

MN202611_1u2jekwcb1q.t:
Andrei Chibis's wife rejects the allegations and he is expected to appear in court on Thursday

The governor of Russia's northern Murmansk region has been arrested on corruption charges in the first detention of a regional leader for five years.

Andrei Chibis, 47, is suspected of embezzlement and misappropriation of more than a billion roubles ($12.2.m; £9.3m) set aside to build an Arctic highway, as well as a further 39m roubles from the Murmansk construction budget.

Chibis is reported to have been detained as he arrived on a visit to Moscow on Monday and was taken in for questioning.

He denies wrongdoing but has made no public comment. His wife Yevgenia Chibis said "anyone who knows our family understands how ridiculous this is".

In a post on social media, she said her husband sincerely believed in the Murmansk region and thanked people for their words of support: "We really need them right now."

Chibis worked for several years as deputy minister for construction and housing, before becoming governor of Murmansk in 2019.

Murmansk is a key military point for Russia in the Arctic and is home to the Russian navy's Northern fleet.

The port of Murmansk is home to the Russian navy's Northern fleet

Chibis was re-elected two years ago after surviving a knife attack and is considered an active supporter of Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Governors are seen as representing the Kremlin, and Vladimir Putin removed several in the months after the war began in February 2022.

However, until now no regional governor has been arrested since the start of the war, even though plenty of high-ranking officials have been detained in that time.

The Murmansk governor is one of a number of officials suspected of corruption by the Russian interior ministry's investigative department which, according to reports, alleged that a criminal group was set up in 2022 to embezzle money from the regional budget and move it abroad, including to Kyrgyzstan.

Another part of the case involves alleged fraud surrounding the rebuilding of a motorway between the two Arctic towns of Apatity and Kirovsk, which are 15km (9.3 miles) apart.

According to Russian news agency Interfax, a court will decide whether Chibis will remain in custody at a hearing on Wednesday.

He has been sanctioned by both the UK and EU, which accuses him of involvement in the illegal transportation of Ukrainian children to Russia and their adoption by Russian families.

MN202611_17afvx7ebv.t:
Matt and Luke Goss will play 10 shows across the UK in 2027

The band Bros have announced their first tour in a decade.

Formed in Camberley, Surrey, in 1986 by twin brothers Matt and Luke Goss alongside Craig Logan, the band had hits including When Will I Be Famous?, Drop The Boy and I Owe You Nothing.

Logan left in 1989 and Bros split three years later, although Matt and Luke Goss reunited in 2017 and have not toured together since.

The 10-date tour in 2027 will include a Wembley Arena show, 38 years after Bros played to 77,000 fans at Wembley Stadium, where they became the youngest act to headline the venue at the age of 20.

The pair will perform across November and December in London, Portsmouth, Birmingham, Sheffield, Brighton, Bath, Derby, Glasgow, Newcastle and Manchester.

Bros debut album Push achieved quadruple-platinum status in the UK and reached number one in Japan and New Zealand.

They also had five UK top five singles in 1988, with eight UK Top 10 hits across their career.

Matt Goss went on to pursue a solo career, releasing five albums, and competed on Strictly Come Dancing in 2022.

A funeral was held earlier in southern Gaza for three Palestinians killed in an Israeli strike

An Israeli air strike has killed the head of Hamas's internal security service in Gaza.

Gaza's Hamas-run interior ministry said Naeem Abu Nahel was targeted by an aircraft in western Gaza City. The 50-year-old had only been in the position since September, when his predecessor was captured in a raid by Israeli special forces .

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz announced that Abu Nahel had been "eliminated" by the Israeli military.

Earlier, Palestinian first responders and health officials reported that six other people had been killed in two Israeli air strikes elsewhere in Gaza on Tuesday.

Three people, including a teenage boy, were killed in the Wadi Gaza area, south of Gaza City, they said. The other three, including two police officers, were killed in a separate strike on a police station in the al-Mawasi area, west of Khan Younis, they added.

Gaza's police force, which operates under the interior ministry, condemned the second attack, saying it was "part of an ongoing campaign targeting the police apparatus aimed at sowing chaos" in the territory.

The Israeli military said it had "struck terrorists in the area".

Israeli strikes on Gaza take place almost daily despite a US-brokered ceasefire agreed by Israel and Hamas in October last year.

At least 1,679 people have been killed in Gaza since then, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel says six of its soldiers have been killed in Gaza over the same period.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,740 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza, the health ministry says.

Hey Duggee is among the shows which will be part of the CBeebies hub on Netflix

The BBC and Netflix are to launch a trial hub on the streaming service next month, featuring 24 CBeebies shows.

Programmes including Hey Duggee, Numberblocks and Teletubbies can be seen on a branded CBeebies hub on Netflix from 2 December.

The trial's aim is to test new ways for the flagship pre-school channel to reach audiences. The BBC is the UK's largest commissioner of children's content.

BBC iPlayer will remain the home for all CBeebies content. Some CBeebies shows such as Shaun the Sheep are already available on Netflix, but this is the first time they will have a home hub on the subscription streamer.

CBeebies shows will also be made available to Netflix members outside the UK in a distribution deal managed by BBC Studios, with the aim of driving investment into children's content in the UK. The deal does not include China.

Netflix will also commit to funding a small number of new CBeebies commissions, the BBC said.

BBC's chief content officer Kate Phillips said the corporation is "always looking at how we can help more audiences discover" its content and brands.

"This limited trial will make a curated selection of CBeebies programmes available on Netflix, while BBC iPlayer remains the home of the full CBeebies experience," she added.

Anne Mensah, vice president of Netflix's UK content said the "unique partnership allows us to work hand in hand with the BBC to support our brilliant British kids' programme makers".

She added: "We want to build a fun and safe space parents can feel good about, with content their kids will love."

The news comes against the backdrop of big changes at the BBC.

The corporation announced plans earlier this year to cut about 1,800 roles and close some programmes and services, but it has further savings to make to reach a £500m savings target.

The BBC's finances have declined in recent years as a result of falling licence fee income and rising production costs.

The corporation also faces growing competition for audiences from streaming services, gaming, social media and YouTube.

The New Spires in Coventry was one of the busiest Marston's pubs in the country during this summer's World Cup

Pub company Marston's has said an "excellent World Cup" helped drive stronger trading as annual profits rose by nearly a fifth, despite reporting a dip in sales .

The Wolverhampton-based firm, which operates more than 1,300 pubs across the UK, reported underlying pre-tax profits of £85.4m for the year to 26 September, up 18.4% from a year earlier.

The company said trading was improved by new-look pubs, strong trade during this summer's football World Cup, and a partnership with Jeremy Clarkson's Hawkstone drinks brand.

"For the third year running, profit is significantly up, cash flow is strong and margins have improved," said chief executive Justin Platt.

The pub chain also said bookings for Christmas events were 9% ahead of the same point last year.

Marston's has invested heavily in refurbishing pubs into new formats, including its sports-focused "Grandstand" venues.

It plans at least 100 more conversions in the new financial year, in a bid to accelerate sales growth further.

One of the busiest locals during the World Cup was The New Spires in Coventry, which reopened in March following a £400,000 makeover.

The New Spires in Coventry reopened in March following a £400,000 conversion to a "Grandstand" venue

The World Cup had been "very full on," said pub partner Pip Sullivan, explaining that on one match night alone they took more than £25,000 over the bar.

Marston's said it had selected the venue for investment because of its involvement with local sports teams, community groups, and charities.

"We've got two football teams, four darts teams and a dominoes team," explained Sullivan, all of which had also helped bolster sales.

But she recognised not all businesses were thriving.

"It's been a difficult year for a lot of pubs and we have empathised as they've lost a lot of trade," she said.

But investment by the company had brought the pub "back to life", she continued.

"We've managed to keep as much custom as we possibly can and seen new custom."

A partnership with Jeremy Clarkson also helped drive profits, said the company

Marston's also pointed to events and promotions, including darts champion Luke Humphries' darts nights and the partnership with Clarkson.

"Guest satisfaction levels have improved again, thanks to the amazing work of our pub teams, whose passion and commitment keep our pubs at the heart of every local community they serve," added Platt.

"Our new pub formats are performing especially well and are now a proven growth engine for the business, giving us real confidence to accelerate our investment plans in 2027."

Nurses will take action short of strike action from 3 December, with a date for full strike action to be confirmed

Nurses in Northern Ireland have voted overwhelmingly to take industrial action, including strike action, over pay.

They will take continuous action short of strike from 3 December - this sort of action includes working to rule and a ban on overtime.

The Royal College of Nursing (RCN) said it was working with other unions for a collective day of strike action, which one its leaders said would probably be early January.

The RCN said the industrial action was the result of the failure of the Northern Ireland Executive and Department of Health to implement the 2026-27 pay award.

A pay review body recommended a 3.3% rise for Agenda for Change staff, which includes nurses, health visitors, midwives, ambulance staff, porters and cleaners, from April this year.

While nursing staff in England and Wales have received their pay awards, nurses in Northern Ireland are still waiting for theirs.

RCN members working in health and social care can now be expected on the picket lines again, seven years after voting yes to taking strike action for the first time in Northern Ireland .

The union said 93% of its members who responded , voted to take action short of strike and strike action.

Rita Devlin, executive director of the RCN in Northern Ireland, said nursing staff were being left behind

Prof Rita Devlin, executive director of the RCN in Northern Ireland, said the result sent "an unequivocal message" to the Northern Ireland Executive and the Department of Health that nursing staff would "no longer tolerate this annual cycle of uncertainty, delay and disregard when it comes to their pay".

She said nursing staff in Northern Ireland were being left behind "because of a failure to provide the necessary funding".

Devlin said members were "being forced into industrial action" to secure the pay award they are due, rather than being focused solely on delivering patient care.

"Nursing staff do not take the decision to strike lightly," she said.

"They understand better than anyone the challenges facing our health service and the impact industrial action can have.

"But they have reached a point where they feel they have no other option."

As winter pressure are building across the health and social care system, Devlin said the last place nurses want to be is on a picket line.

"Responsibility for this situation sits squarely with our political leaders, who have once again failed to ensure nursing staff are treated fairly and paid on time," she added.

Sadio Mane's Senegal have been confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners following their appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport, giving the Teranga Lions a second continental title

Senegal have been reinstated as winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) after a ruling by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas).

The court's award overturns a previous decision which had stripped the West Africans of the title they won on the pitch during a chaotic final against host nation Morocco in January.

The result of that match in Rabat, which saw the Teranga Lions triumph 1-0 after extra time, was overturned almost two months later when a Confederation of African Football (Caf) appeals board decreed Senegal had breached competition regulations by leaving the field of play in second-half stoppage time in protest at a penalty awarded against them.

Senegal's football federation (FSF) subsequently appealed to Cas, sport's highest legal authority, with a three-man panel hearing its case behind closed doors in Lausanne on 8 October.

In a unanimous verdict, the Cas panel has effectively backed the decision by referee Jean-Jacques Ndala to restart the game after Senegal returned to the field and the match was played to a conclusion. The result of the final stands and Senegal are now confirmed as Afcon 2025 winners.

The court said it considered that "the referee's decision to resume the match or to stop it fell definitively within his sole authority".

"By blowing his whistle to restart play, the referee considered that the conditions for resuming the match had been met - both teams were on the pitch again, and both expressed their willingness to resume."

The FSF immediately reacted with a social media post featuring a picture of the side lifting the trophy in January captioned with the phrase "again and always".

Caf is yet to comment on the decision but its president Patrice Motsepe has repeatedly said that his organisation will respect and adhere to the Cas ruling.

Morocco's football federation (FRMF) is also yet to comment on the verdict.

Morocco and Senegal have both changed coach since the final and earlier this month secured their places at the 2027 edition of the tournament with two rounds of qualification remaining.

This ruling should now settle any debate about who the history books will recognise as continental champions - although plenty in Morocco may not agree with the outcome of the case at Cas.

KIGALI – Rwanda is seeking to move its cycling strategy beyond Tour du Rwanda by expanding local competitions, developing young riders and creating more opportunities for women in a sport whose visibility has largely revolved around its flagship race.

The shift was outlined during the inaugural Rwanda Cycling Day, introduced by the Rwanda Cycling Federation (FERWACY) to celebrate achievements across the sport and present its plans for the future.

“For so many years, we thought of this day as only about Tour du Rwanda unveiling the next edition. But Rwandan cycling is beyond one event. So today marks the beginning of an event where we will be celebrating what we have achieved within the whole year and unveiling the future,” said Jean Hubert Ishimwe, FERWACY President.

One of the changes concerns the format of Tour du Rwanda, which will retain its eight-day program but allocate six days to the stage race and two to one-day classic competitions.

Ishimwe said the adjustment is intended to add more value to the event and broaden the competition program.

“Usually we knew Tour du Rwanda as 8 days, but this time around, Tour du Rwanda will be 6 days and reserve those 2 days for classic races. We thought of another way to add value to Tour du Rwanda. We thought about trophies,” he said.

The federation also unveiled a new trophy inspired by Rwanda’s local context, with a design intended to reflect the country’s identity as the Land of a Thousand Hills.

“We wanted something unique, something local, this Ikoro is from our local context. The gold finish represents the honor of winning, resilience and the fighting spirit required in cycling.,” Ishimwe said.

The next Tour du Rwanda will cover 1,023 kilometers, with a reported cumulative elevation gain of 17,200 meters. Eugene Uwambaje, FERWACY Technical Director, said the route would combine difficult climbs, descents and new roads.

“It’s not going to be an easy Tour du Rwanda, but it will be mixed with many hills, descending and new roads,” he said.

Beyond the flagship race, FERWACY has focused on developing young cyclists through the Youth Racing Cup, launched in 2024 in partnership with the Union Cycliste Internationale (UCI).

The program was established ahead of the 2025 UCI Road World Championships in Kigali, giving children opportunities to participate in organized races and gain competitive experience.

Ishimwe said the initiative was already producing results after two years, describing the young riders as the foundation for the sport’s future.

“These kids are the products of our youth development. To simply say, we are laying a strong foundation and then it is going to be the key pillar where we are going to build everything we are building,” he said.

The Ministry of Sports also wants more competitions organized locally to improve the performance of Rwandan athletes.

Dr. Brave Olivier Ngabo, Permanent Secretary in the Ministry of Sports, said hosting international events should go hand in hand with developing local talent.

“We want to have more competition locally, because it’s not about only the success of preparation, something that we are getting to be known about as a country, but also the upgrade of the level of athletes,” he said.

FERWACY has also sought to create stronger pathways for female cyclists, particularly those aiming to compete internationally. Ange Belyse Umuhoza, the federation’s Second Vice President, said expanding opportunities for women was part of the effort to strengthen the sport.

“We are now extending this opportunity to women, creating stronger platforms for female athletes, particularly in Africa, to compete, develop and shine internationally,” she said.

The plans point to a broader effort to build a cycling program that offers more than an annual international race. More local competitions, youth development and opportunities for women will be important in determining whether Rwanda can translate its growing profile in cycling into stronger domestic competition.

The 19th edition of Tour du Rwanda will take place from February 19 to 28, 2027, featuring two one-day classic races alongside the six-stage international tour. The opening classic, covering 111 kilometers from Gicumbi to Nyamata, is scheduled for February 19, followed by an amateur race on February 20.

The six stages will run from February 21 to 26. The program will conclude with the second classic, a 118.2-kilometre race around Kigali, on February 28. In total, the three competitions will cover approximately 1,023 kilometers.

Millwall have been ordered to play a future Championship match in front of a partially-closed stadium as punishment for fans' discriminatory chants.

The club has also been fined £70,000 by a Football Association disciplinary panel, and been told another offence this season will lead to a further partial stadium closure.

The sanctions were imposed for ableist and homophobic chants, heard at a game against Charlton Athletic in January.

"These chants are discriminatory, unacceptable, and will not be tolerated at The Den or anywhere Millwall play," Millwall's managing director Mark Fairbrother said in an open letter to supporters. , external

"Incidents like this hurt all of us, but none more so than people who are directly discriminated against by ableist, homophobic or other unacceptable chanting, and we apologise to anybody that was affected, offended or impacted by the chants."

Blocks 19, 20, 47 and 48 of the Dockers Stand - the two-tiered east stand at The Den - will have to be closed for one game.

The sanction is effective 14 days from the date of the decision, meaning the closure is likely to be imposed for the Championship fixture against Sheffield United on 8 December.

The club can request for the 14-day period to be extended if the closure cannot be implemented safely in time.

Iyi raporo igaragaza ko kugira ubumenyi bw'ibanze bukomeye ari byo bituma ubumenyi mu ikoranabuhanga n'ibidukikije butanga umusaruro.

Imbaraga u Rwanda rwashyize mu gufasha abanyeshuri kuziba icyuho cy'ubumenyi cyatewe n'icyorezo cya COVID-19, no kwinjiza amasomo yo gukora porogaramu za mudasobwa n'ubwenge buhangano (AI) mu mashuri, zagaragajwe nk'ingero nziza ibindi bihugu bya Afurika byakwigiraho muri raporo nshya ku burezi bw'amashuri yisumbuye.

Raporo ya Mastercard Foundation yiswe Secondary Education in Africa: Expanding Pathways to Work, Livelihoods, and Lifelong Learning (Uburezi bw'amashuri yisumbuye muri Afurika: Kwagura inzira zigana ku mirimo, imibereho myiza no gukomeza kwiga ubuzima bwose), yamuritswe i Accra muri Ghana ku wa Kabiri, imbere y'abaminisitiri b'uburezi, imiryango nyafurika, abashakashatsi, abarimu n'urubyiruko.

U Rwanda ni kimwe mu bihugu birindwi byakoreweho ubushakashatsi bwimbitse mu gutegura iyi raporo, kandi urubyiruko rw'u Rwanda na rwo rwagize uruhare mu bushakashatsi.

Perezida akaba n'Umuyobozi Mukuru wa Mastercard Foundation, Sewit Ahderom, yagize ati: “Uburezi bw'urubyiruko rw'iki gihe, cyane cyane ku rwego rw'amashuri yisumbuye, bugomba kurugeza ku ntego runaka. Ku rubyiruko rwinshi rwo muri Afurika, amashuri yisumbuye ni yo mahirwe ya nyuma gahunda z'uburezi ziba zifite yo kurugeraho ku bwinshi.”

Yongeyeho ati: “Ni ho dushobora kugira uruhare rukomeye mu gutuma rubona akazi karubereye, gatanga icyubahiro kandi karushimisha.”

Gufasha buri munyeshuri kuzuza icyuho cy'ubumenyi

Nyuma y'icyorezo cya COVID-19, u Rwanda rwashyizeho gahunda y'igihugu yo gufasha abanyeshuri kuzuza icyuho cy'ubumenyi no gusubira ku murongo (Remedial and Catch-Up Program), igenewe abanyeshuri bafite ibyago byo gusibira cyangwa guta ishuri, haba mu mashuri abanza ndetse no mu cyiciro rusange cy'amashuri yisumbuye.

Iyi gahunda yashyizwe mu bikorwa binyuze mu mabwiriza ya Leta ateganya ko buri munyeshuri asuzumwa mu kwezi kwa mbere kw'amashuri, hagakurikiraho amasomo y'inyongera ya buri cyumweru, hashingiwe ku byo buri munyeshuri akeneye.

Mu mashuri yisumbuye, akenshi byakorwaga hifashishijwe isomo rya mbere ry'icyumweru muri buri somo ry'ingenzi, rigenerwa gufasha abanyeshuri kuziba icyuho cy'ubumenyi. Byongeye kandi, buri wa Gatanu mu gitondo hatangwaga amasomo y'inyongera mu mibare n'Icyongereza.

Urwego rw'Igihugu rushinzwe Uburezi bw'Ibanze (REB) rwatanze inyoborabarezi zifasha abarimu gutegura no gutanga ayo masomo.

Raporo igaragaza ko nubwo hataraba isuzuma ryuzuye ry'iyi gahunda, umubare w'abanyeshuri basibira wagabanutse mu mashuri yashyize mu bikorwa iyi gahunda neza.

Gukemura iki kibazo ni ngombwa. Raporo ivuga ko mu bizamini bisoza amashuri yisumbuye byakozwe mu 2023, abanyeshuri 47% gusa ari bo bageze ku bipimo by'ubumenyi by'igihugu mu Cyongereza, 64% mu mibare na 65% mu bumenyi bw'isi n'ibidukikije (Science).

Eunice Muthengi, Umuyobozi ushinzwe Ubushakashatsi n'Isesengura ry'Ubushishozi ku Burezi muri Mastercard Foundation, watanze ibyavuye muri iyi raporo, yagize ati: “Kugera ku burezi ntibiba byemejwe gusa igihe umwana atangiye ishuri. Bigomba gukomeza kurindwa no gushyigikirwa muri buri cyiciro gikomeye cy'inzira y'uburezi.”

Porogaramu za mudasobwa, ubwenge buhangano n'amashuri arengera ibidukikije Raporo inagaragaza u Rwanda, hamwe na Kenya, mu bihugu byatangiye kwigisha abanyeshuri bo mu mashuri yisumbuye gukora porogaramu za mudasobwa (computer programming).

Muri Nyakanga 2025, Minisiteri y'Uburezi n'Urwego rw'Igihugu rushinzwe Uburezi bw'Ibanze batangije gahunda y'igihugu igamije kwinjiza ubumenyi ku bwenge buhangano (AI) mu nteganyanyigisho z'ikoranabuhanga n'itumanaho (ICT) mu mashuri abanza no mu cyiciro rusange cy'amashuri yisumbuye.

Ikigo cy'Igihugu cy'Indashyikirwa mu Kwigisha no Kwiga Gukora Porogaramu za Mudasobwa (Rwanda Coding Academy) na cyo gihugura abanyeshuri mu bijyanye no gukora porogaramu za mudasobwa n'ubwubatsi bw'ikoranabuhanga (software engineering).

Raporo isobanura ko izi ari intambwe zikomeye, dore ko isesengura ryakorewe mu bihugu 49 byo munsi y'Ubutayu bwa Sahara ryagaragaje ko ibihugu bibiri gusa ari byo byinjije ku buryo bweruye amasomo ajyanye n'ubwenge buhangano mu nteganyanyigisho zabyo, mu gihe amashuri yisumbuye atageze kuri kimwe cya kabiri muri Afurika ari yo afite internet.

Muthengi yagize ati: “Ikoranabuhanga si inzira y'ubusamo yo kwirengagiza ibibazo by'inzego z'uburezi. Ritanga umusaruro mwiza iyo riri mu bigize impinduka zagutse kandi rigafasha abarimu aho kubasimbura.”

Urubyiruko rukeneye ubuyobozi n'ubumenyi ku ikoreshwa ry'ikoranabuhanga, kimwe n'ibikoresho byaryo.

Umwe mu banyeshuri bo muri Ghana bagize uruhare mu bushakashatsi yagize ati: “Dukeneye kumenya igihe bikwiriye gukoresha ubwenge buhangano (AI) n'igihe tugomba gukora imirimo twifashishije ubushobozi bwacu bwite.”

Paul Kasanga, Umuyobozi w'agateganyo wa Mastercard Foundation muri Ghana, ni we watangaje aya magambo mu birori byo kumurika raporo.

Umwarimu na we yagize ati: “Twe abarimu muri rusange twiteguye kwakira no gukoresha ikoranabuhanga rishya, ariko dukeneye guhugurwa kugira ngo turusheho kugira ubumenyi burikenewe.”

U Rwanda rwakoze kandi ibikorwa bigamije guteza imbere amashuri arengera ibidukikije (Eco-Schools). Iyi gahunda yatangijwe mu 2020 ku bufatanye bw'Urwego rw'Igihugu rushinzwe Uburezi bw'Ibanze, Ikigo cy'Igihugu gishinzwe Kubungabunga Ibidukikije (REMA) n'Umuryango Albertine Rift Conservation Society, hagamijwe kongerera abanyeshuri ubumenyi ku mihindagurikire y'ikirere binyuze mu bikorwa bitandukanye bidasanzwe mu masomo asanzwe.

Minisitiri w'Uburezi w'u Rwanda, Nyakubahwa Joseph Nsengimana, yagize ati: “Amashuri asanzwe ntashobora kuba yo yonyine atanga amahirwe yo gutera imbere. Guverinoma zigomba kwemera, gutanga impamyabumenyi no guteza imbere inzira zinyuranye z'uburezi zinoze kandi zorohereza abantu kwiga, kugira ngo zibe ubundi buryo bwuzuzanya kandi bugize gahunda z'uburezi.” Abarimu ni bo shingiro ry'impinduka

Raporo ishimangira ko nta na kimwe muri ibi bikorwa gishobora gutanga umusaruro udashyigikiwe n'abarimu.

U Rwanda ruri mu bihugu biri kuvugurura amahugurwa y'abarimu kugira ngo ajyane n'integanyanyigisho zishingiye ku bushobozi bw'umunyeshuri (Competency-Based Curriculum), nk'uko raporo ibigaragaza.

Impinduka ziheruka mu burezi bw'u Rwanda ziteganya ko amasomo yo mu cyiciro cya kabiri cy'amashuri yisumbuye agabanywa mu byiciro byagutse by'inzira z'amasomo (learning pathways), mu gihe amasomo rusange ahuriweho n'abanyeshuri bose akomeza kubahirizwa.

Ahderom yagize ati: “Abarimu ni bo bahindura ibitekerezo byanditse ku mpapuro bikaba ubunararibonye umwana ahura na bwo mu buzima busanzwe, kandi dukeneye kubashyigikira.”

Minisitiri w'Uburezi wa Ghana, Nyakubahwa Haruna Iddrisu, wayoboye ibirori byo kumurika iyi raporo, na we yagize ati: “Kumenya niba amahirwe yo kwiga ahinduka koko ubumenyi, ahanini bishingira ku mutungo wacu ukomeye kurusha indi yose ari wo barimu. Iyi raporo igaragaza neza ko kubaka abakozi bafite ubumenyi, ubushake n'ubushobozi bwo gukora ari ingenzi kugira ngo tugere ku mpinduka zifatika.”

Ku rwego rw'umugabane wa Afurika, urubyiruko rugera kuri miliyoni 77 ruri mu kigero cy'imyaka yo kwiga mu mashuri yisumbuye ntiruri mu mashuri. Byongeye kandi, ibihugu byo munsi y'Ubutayu bwa Sahara bikenera abarimu bashya b'amashuri yisumbuye bagera kuri miliyoni 10.7 bitarenze umwaka wa 2030.

Mu byifuzo bitandatu by'ingenzi iyi raporo itanga harimo kwigisha abarimu n'abanyeshuri ubumenyi mu ikoranabuhanga n'ubwenge buhangano (AI), gushora imari mu burezi bw'ibanze no mu masomo afasha abanyeshuri kuzuza icyuho cy'ubumenyi, ndetse no gushyiraho ihuriro riyobowe na za Guverinoma rigamije guteza imbere uburezi bw'amashuri yisumbuye muri Afurika.

Ahderom yagize ati: “Mastercard Foundation yiyemeje gukorana na za Guverinoma n'abafatanyabikorwa kugira ngo ibimenyetso n'ubushakashatsi byagaragajwe bihindurwe ibikorwa bifatika, bityo urubyiruko rusoze amashuri rufite ubushobozi bwo kwibeshaho no kubaka ahazaza hashingiwe ku mahitamo yarwo.” IHEREZO

Syrians coming back after the war are falling victim to mines and other explosives

Eleven-year-old Alaa was tending her family's goats with her siblings in a field behind their home in Umm Khuzaym, north-west Syria, on Sunday when there was a flash and a deafening bang.

"Then we heard people screaming," Alaa's father, Walid Mohammed Al-Ghafar, told the BBC.

Walid ran outside to find his daughter lying face down, killed, and her 10-year-old brother, Mahmoud, seriously injured.

Unwittingly, the children had triggered a landmine.

The incident and others this week bring to nearly 1,000 the number of children killed or injured by explosive ordnance in Syria since the fall of Bashar al-Assad in December 2024, according to the UN Mine Action Service (Unmas).

The village is one of many where families have returned to homes and farmland that were once on the front lines of Syria's 13-year civil war.

Alaa's father said demining teams had visited several times to clear the fields. He and other residents believed it was safe for farmers and children to move around.

But mines and other explosives can lie far beyond former battle lines, making it difficult to establish which areas are safe.

"Remnants of war from today's conflicts are often very widely and broadly scattered, often without patterns, which makes it extremely difficult to do clearance," Katrin Atkins, research lead at Landmine Monitor, a global mine monitoring initiative, told the BBC.

The dangers are reflected in a sharp rise in casualties across Syria.

A total of 1,602 people were killed or injured by landmines and explosive remnants of war in 2025 alone, an increase of more than 50% on the previous year, according to the Landmine Monitor report, published by the International Campaign to Ban Landmines on Tuesday.

Only Myanmar, with 1,891 casualties, recorded more.

The report attributes the rise in Syria partly to the large-scale return of refugees and internally displaced people following Assad's overthrow.

"When you look at population movement, a couple of months later you see an increase of incidents in these areas, because that's exactly where people go and start to use the fields again," Atkins said.

More than 60% of casualties recorded by the world's largest landmine clearance charity, the Halo Trust, involve farming, agriculture or shepherding, according to its Syria programme manager, Simon Jackson.

"They're not going to wait for the government or for organisations like us to come and tell them that everything is safe and clear," he told the BBC. "People are taking risks out of desperation."

Since Assad's fall on 8 December 2024, Unmas has recorded at least 1,556 incidents in Syria involving explosive ordnance.

They have caused 2,701 casualties: 935 people killed and 1,766 injured. Children account for 995 of those victims, or about 37%.

But the toll is likely to be higher, with experts estimating that overall casualties could be under-reported by 25-50%.

Both government forces and rebels laid land mines during the civil war

For many of those who survive, the consequences are devastating and permanent.

Majid Abdul Rahman, 27, was travelling in a car in the Ghouta region on the outskirts of Damascus in March 2025 when it struck an explosive device. The vehicle filled with smoke and he felt a pain in his leg.

More than a year later, Majid has difficulty walking and has been unable to return to work, leaving him struggling to provide for his family.

The danger has continued into this month, with at least 20 people killed and more than 40 injured by explosive ordnance in November.

In one of the worst recorded incidents, an explosion in a school courtyard in Hasakah on 4 November killed a 12-year-old and injured 19 others. And on Monday, a 13-year-old boy was killed when an unexploded cluster munition detonated in southern Daraa province.

The threat is also holding back Syria's economic recovery. Contaminated farmland cannot be safely cultivated, while people collecting scrap metal or trying to salvage materials from abandoned areas also risk triggering explosions.

The Syrian Ministry of Defence says since the end of 2024 its teams have found and dealt with more than 315,000 mines and unexploded munitions.

But no nationwide survey has established how much land remains contaminated, making it difficult to assess the full scale of the problem.

"We're in a bit of a black hole," Atkins said.

And with the extent of contamination still largely unknown, the war continues to claim victims two years after it ended.

Nkuko byatangajwe n’ibinyamakuru mpuzamahanga bicukumbura siporo, byemeje ko Ikipe y’igihugu ya Senegal yasubijwe igikombe cyayo cy’Afurika yatsindiye mu kibuga nyuma yo gutsinda Morocco ku mukino wa nyuma wabaye muri Mutarama uyu mwaka.

Uru rukiko rukuru nkemurampaka ku isi (TAS) rwatesheje agaciro icyemezo cyari cyarafashwe n'Impuzamashyirahamwe y'Umupira w'Amaguru muri Afurika (CAF), rwemeza ko Sénégal ari yo yegukanye igikombe ku mugaragaro.

Taliki ya 18 Mutarama 2026, nibwo hakinwe umukino wa nyuma w’igikombe cy’Afurika cya cya 2025, i Rabat ho muri Maroke ari nayo yari yakiriye iki gikombe. Ubwo umukino wari urimbanyije, imvururu zatangiye ku munota wa 90+2 w’iminota y’inyongera kuko iminota 90 yari yarangiye ari 0-0.

Umukinnyi w’ikipe ya Senegal Ismaïla Sarr yatsindiye Sénégal igitego n'umutwe, ariko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala acyanga avuga ko myugariro wa Sénégal, Abdoulaye Seck, yari yakoreye ikosa Achraf Hakimi mbere y'uko igitego kijyamo. Nyuma y'iminota mike gusa, rutahizamu wa Maroke, Brahim Díaz, yaguye mu rubuga rw'amahina nyuma yo gukorwaho ikosa na El Hadji Malick Diouf. Umusifuzi nyuma yo kwitabaza ikoranabuhanga rya VAR maze yemeza ko ari penaliti ya Maroc.

Kubera uburakari bw'igitego cyabo cyari cyanzwe n'iyo penaliti babonaga ko itari ikwiye, umutoza wa Sénégal, Pape Thiaw, yahise asaba abakinnyi be kuva mu kibuga. Bamwe mu bakinnyi basubiye mu rwambariro, umukino uhagarara iminota igera kuri 14.

ku munota 90+23’, Nyuma yo kwingingwa cyane na kapiteni wabo Sadio Mané wasanze bagenzi be mu rwambariro akabasaba kugaruka kurangiza umukino, abakinnyi ba Sénégal baragarutse maze Brahim Díaz atera ya penaliti (mu buryo bwa Panenka)ku bw’amahirwe macye ya Maroke ifatwa neza n'umunyezamu Édouard Mendy.

umukino waramoje maze Pape Gueye ku mupira wari uvuye kuri Idrissa Gana Gueye, atera ishoti rikomeye cyane n'akaguru k'ibumoso rigana mu nguni yo hejuru y'izamu rya Yassine Bounou maze Senegal itsinda igitego cya mbere ari nacyo cyasoje umukino maze Senegal yegukana Igikombe ityo.

Ntabwo byarangiriye aho kuko taliki ya 17 Werurwe 2026 nyuma y’ubujurire bwa Maroke (FRMF) ,Akanama k'Ubujurire ka CAF kemeje ko Sénégal yatewe mpaga kubera kuva mu kibuga nta ruhushya rw'umusifuzi, byatumye ihabwa igihano cyo gutsindwa ibitego 3-0 maze maroke igahabwa igikombe cy’ Afuria cya 2025. Ubujurire bwa Sénégal muri TAS

Taliki ya wa 25 Werurwe 2026, Ishyirahamwe ry'Umupira w'Amaguru muri Sénégal (FSF) ryatanze ikirego muri TAS risaba ko icyemezo cya CAF gitesha agaciro Sénégali ikagumana igikombe cyayo yegukanye itsinze Maroke. Senegare yatanze ikirego ishingiye ku ngingo ivuga ko amategeko y'umupira w'amaguru ateganya ko icyemezo cy'umusifuzi mu kibuga ari ntakuka, kandi ko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala yemeye ko umukino ukomeza kugeza urangiye.

Taliki ya 8 Ukwakira 2026, TAS yaburanishije urubanza rwaburanishijwe mu muhezo i Lausanne mu Busuwisi rukaba rwaramaze amasaha arenga atanu ruhuza abahagarariye Sénégal, Maroc ndetse na CAF.

Amategeko agenga imikino ya CAN niya FIFA ni yo yari ku isonga mu byaranze uru rubanza rwa Sénégal, Maroc, na CAF muri TAS. Impande zombi zashingiraga cyane ku ngingo zivuguruzanya hagati y’ububasha bw’umusifuzi mu kibuga n’ibihano biteganywa iyo ikipe ivuye mu kibuga.

1. Ingingo Sénégal yishingikirizaho (Ububasha bw'umusifuzi)

•Itegeko rya 5 rya FIFA (Laws of the Game - Law 5). Iri tegeko rivuga ko ibyemezo by'umusifuzi mu kibuga ku bijyanye n'imigendekere y'umukino ari ntakuka kandi ko umukino uba warangiye iyo umusifuzi awushoje ku mugaragaro. Sénégal ivuga ko umusifuzi Jean-Jacques Ndala atasoje umukino ngo atange mpaga, ahubwo yakomeje umukino kugeza urangiye.

•Ihame ryo kutaburanisha ibyabaye mu kibuga (Field of Play Doctrine). Urukiko rwa TAS rusanzwe rufite ihame ryo kutivanga mu byemezo by'abasifuzi byafatiwe mu kibuga mu gihe umukino ukomeje, keretse iyo hari ibimenyetso bya ruswa cyangwa uburiganya.

2. Ingingo Maroc na CAF bishingikirizaho (Guta ikibuga / Abandonment)

•Ingingo ya 82 n'iya 84 z'amategeko agenga CAN (AFCON Regulations). Aya mategeko asobanura neza ko ikipe yose ivuye mu kibuga idahawe uburenganzira n'umusifuzi, cyangwa ikanga gukomeza umukino, ifatwa nk'iyikuye mu irushanwa maze igaterwa mpaga (forfeit) y'ibitego 3-0.

•Amategeko y'imyitwarire ya CAF (CAF Disciplinary Code - Ingingo ya 148). Maroc ivuga ko kuba abakinnyi ba Sénégal baramaze iminota 14 hanze y'ikibuga byahungabanyije umukino mu buryo butemewe n'amategeko, bityo Akanama k'Ubujurire ka CAF kari gafite ububasha bwo gufata icyemezo nyuma y'umukino gashingiye kuri raporo y'umusifuzi n'iya komiseri w'umukino.

MN202611_198yxk0quym.t:
Debbie Hewitt has been chair at the FA since 2022

Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt has signed a non-disclosure agreement (NDA) as a condition of viewing documents related to Fifa president Gianni Infantino's failed World Cup sell-off plot.

Hewitt was granted access to the information at the world governing body's headquarters in Zurich.

Earlier this month, Fifa said "key documents" on the abandoned plan to sell stakes in its tournaments to private investors would be made available to members of its council, but only in person and under "strict review protocols to preserve confidentiality".

Uefa had demanded Fifa release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and answer questions relating to its decision-making.

Hewitt was among a group of council members who wrote to Fifa to say they were "concerned that any review would seemingly be limited to certain 'key documents'… which in turn would only be available for review under unknown 'strict review protocols'".

They also asked for clarity on what the protocols were, and "an explanation as to why Fifa considers such restrictions necessary since it is not clear why our rights are being limited in such a way".

The NDA means Hewitt cannot reveal what she has read, or comment about it publicly.

Hewitt has previously criticised Infantino for a lack of transparency.

However, she embraced the Fifa president at a ceremony in Zurich on Monday when the UK bid to host the 2035 Women's World Cup was ratified at a special ceremony.

It is unclear whether she viewed the files on the same day, and which documents have been made available.

Last week, BBC Sport revealed the FA had considered challenging Infantino's eligibility to run for a fourth term as Fifa president, and that it is backing French candidate Philippe Diallo in next year's presidential election.

Fifa has been approached for comment. Sources have previously indicated Fifa's ability to answer some questions is limited by legal action that Uefa launched in October in the US, requesting disclosure of evidence and documents, warning it could lodge a criminal complaint in Switzerland.

An estimated 5,258 deaths in England were associated with this summer's hot weather

More than 5,000 people suffered heat-associated deaths in England this summer, the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has estimated - the highest number since records began in 2016.

The UK experienced its hottest summer on record in 2026, and the estimated 5,258 heat-linked deaths were twice the previous high of 2,985 in 2022.

The most deadly period of the year for heat-related deaths was between 21 and 28 June, when there were an estimated 2,401 heat-associated deaths. Temperatures peaked at 38C in that period.

Climate change is expected to increase the length, frequency and intensity of extreme heat, the UKHSA has warned.

The UKHSA said summer 2026 was "exceptional", and that it recorded the highest annual number of heat episodes, which it defines as days when the average Central England Temperature (CET) is at least 20C.

There were seven heat episodes between May and August, adding up to a total of 41 days.

The UK experienced widespread heatwaves as 2026 became the hottest summer on record, according to provisional data from the Met Office.

A heatwave in May smashed the temperature record for that month by more than 2C, with a high of 35.1C recorded at Kew Gardens.

A month later, June's heatwave set another monthly temperature record - 38.0C in Lingwood, Norfolk. The previous high was 35.6C set in 1957 and equalled during the infamous 1976 heatwave.

Both were caused by heat domes - stalled areas of high pressure that trap hot air over the region.

Another heatwave in mid-August saw temperatures climb as high as 38.2C at Hartpury College in Gloucestershire, making it the hottest day of the year.

The UK's hottest day on record was 19 July 2022, when temperatures hit 40.3C in Coningsby, Lincolnshire.

A lack of rainfall this year also saw droughts declared in all of Wales and more than two-thirds of England, while wildfires caused devastation in some parts of the country.

UKHSA said the findings "underline the need for longer-term adaptation" to a warming climate, and that adapting homes, neighbourhoods and health and care settings would be "increasingly important".

Dr Ross Thompson, principal environmental health scientist at UKHSA, said this summer's hot weather had a substantial impact on public health, "particularly during the early heat episodes in May and June".

He added that periods of extreme heat are expected to become "longer, more frequent and more intense" as the climate continues to warm.

Speaking in the Commons, Health Secretary Yvette Cooper said she wanted "to offer the deepest condolences to all those who lost a loved one this summer".

"The numbers are a stark reminder of the human impact of climate change, and that is why I have asked the NHS to now prepare for summer as seriously as we do for winter," she said.

During a speech at the COP31 summit earlier this month, Prime Minister Andy Burnham spoke about the extreme weather experienced in the UK this summer, describing it as "not normal".

Leny Yoro was sent off for this tackle on Alexander Isak

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro has had the red card he was shown during Sunday's Premier League match at Liverpool overturned.

The Football Association has confirmed Yoro will now be clear to face Brentford at Old Trafford on Saturday.

"Leny Yoro's one-match suspension has been removed following a successful claim of wrongful dismissal," said the FA in a statement.

New United head coach Mauricio Pochettino was furious at the decision, which came just eight minutes in and, he felt, changed the course of the game, which Liverpool won 4-0.

Liverpool striker Alexander Isak ran on to a ball that bounced over Matthijs de Ligt but took a heavy touch that meant the ball was likely to run through to United goalkeeper Senne Lammens even if Yoro had not brought the Swede down.

Nevertheless, referee Sam Barrott sent Yoro off, drawing criticism from Pochettino.

"The ball wasn't in his control," he said. "Isak, when he saw the control wasn't good, it's normal to delay, and stop to the run. In that moment that Yoro came from the back, and you go down.

"But all that we play football; you know that wasn't intentional. That is never a foul."

'No-one's coming to save us' - but how can Man Utd save themselves?

United have travelled to Lisbon for their next Champions League match on Wednesday (20:00 GMT).

The early dismissal of Yoro at Anfield meant Sporting had no chance to assess any changes Pochettino might have made after he replaced Michael Carrick during the international break.

But despite United sitting 19th in the Premier League, Sporting boss refuses to accept United are "fragile".

"I don't following the reasoning," said Fonseca, who was only appointed on 4 November after the Portuguese club bought him out of his contract at Lyon.

"Manchester is a great team," he said. "I don't believe a lot that great teams are fragile. The last game they played in the Champions League, they were trailing 2-0, then won 3-2 against a very difficult opponent in Roma.

"Moreover, when they have a new head coach, with such world-class players, it's extremely unpredictable to see if they will have a good day or bad day."

United have not won in the Premier League since August and have conceded 19 goals in their past six games in all competitions.

Yet, such was the nature of the Liverpool game, Fonseca has had to watch analysis of Pochettino's time in charge of the United States to get an idea of what to expect.

"Eight minutes, red card. It's impossible to make an analysis," he said.

"I tried to see Pochettino with the United States and what kind of solutions he used. There is some information but it is very difficult to predict."

Gaza yahinduwe "ahantu hasinzikaye cane kandi hahumanye", aho ibice birenga 99% vy'ubutaka bw'Abanyapalestina vyerekana ibimenyetso vy'uko ibidukikije vyahumanijwe n'ibitero vya gisirikare vya Israel, nk'uko bivugwa mu cegeranyo gishasha cashizwe ahabona n'ishirahamwe mpuzamakungu Oxfam.

Muri ico cegeranyo, iryo shirahamwe rivuga ko ubwoko butari buke bw'ibihumanya harimwo ivyuma biremereye, ibisigarira vy'ibisasu vyaturitse, ivy'ivyitwa 'amiante' bikoreshwa mu nyubako, hamwe n'ibindi bisigarira vy'ubumara, biteye akaga ku Banyapalestina muri iki gihe, kandi ko bishobora kuzobandanya bibagirako ingaruka mu myaka mirongo iri imbere.

Amitabh Behar, umuyobozi mukuru wa Oxfam International, yavuze ko ingaruka ivyo vyagize kuri Gaza "zizokwonona cane ibidukikije, ku buryo bitazoba bigishobokera abantu kuhaba neza".

Mu kwishura, ambasade ya Israel mu Bwongereza yavuze ko ico cegeranyo kidakwije "ibisabwa kinyamwuga".

Behar kandi yagirije Israel "ivyaha vyo mu ntambara vyakorewe ibidukikije", avuga ko biri mu bigize "ihonyabwoko rikibandanya muri Gaza".

Israel irahakana ibirego vy'ihonyabwoko mu rubanza rukibandanya muri Sentare Mpuzamakungu y'Ubutungane (ICJ), ivuga ko birimwo irementanya.

Israel ivuga kandi ko ibikorwa vyayo vya gisirikare muri Gaza ari ukwikingira ibitero vya Hamas, mu kwishura igitero casheshe amaraso uwo muhari wagavye ku butaka bwayo ku wa 7 Gitugutu (10) 2023. Ishimangira ko igenda ifata ingingo zo kugabanya ingaruka z'ibitero ku basivire.

Ahavuye isanamu, Anadolu via Getty Images

Amashirahamwe Oxfam hamwe na Conflict and Environment Observatory (CEOBS) rikorera mu Bwongereza rigakurikirana ingaruka z'intambara ku bidukikije, yakoresheje amafoto yafashwe n'ibigendajuru, ubuhinga bwo gukurikirana isi hakoreshejwe ibigendajuru, hamwe n'isesangura ry'ayandi masoko y'amakuru, kugira ngo hasohorwe icegeranyo.

Amakuru ya BBC Gahuza ako kanya kuri WhatsApp yawe

Ico cegeranyo ni co, gushika ubu, gisesangura mu buryo buramvuye kurusha ibindi ingaruka zidasanzwe ku bidukikije zatewe n'intambara ikomeye imaze imyaka itatu ibera muri Gaza.

Kirasesangura ingene ibisasu n'ibindi bikoresho vy'intambara vyakoreshejwe mu bitero bikomeye vya Israel, hamwe n'ibisigarira vy'inyubakwa n'ibikorwa remezo vyasambuwe, vyose vyagize ingaruka ku bidukikije.

Mu kwezi kwa Ruhuhuma (2), umuhinga wa ONU ajejwe ivy'uburenganzira bwa muntu yavuze ko mu kiringo c'imyaka hafi ibiri, ibisasu birenga amatoni 200.000 vyatewe kuri Gaza. Yavuze ko inguvu zavyo zingana n'"inguvu z'ibisasu ruhonyanganda nk'ivyaturikiye i Hiroshima bigera kuri 13".

Mu mwaka uheze, ishami rya ONU rijejwe ibidukikije (UNEP) ryagereranije ko ibikorwa vya gisirikare vya Israel vyasambuye amazu n'ibikorwa remezo bigasigaza ibibomoke n'ibisigarira birenga amatoni miliyoni 61 mu karere kose. Ico cegeranyo kivuga ko hafi 15% vy'ivyo bisigarira bishobora kuba birimwo ibintu bihumanya ibidukikije biteye akaga gakomeye.

Lama Abdul Samad, umwe mu banditse icegeranyo ca Oxfam, yabwiye BBC ati: "Abantu bazohura n'ingaruka z'indwara zidakira ku gihe kirekire, kuko vyinshi muri ivyo bintu bihumanya bigumizwa mu bidukikije igihe kirekire."

Avuga ko Abanyapalestina baba muri Gaza, ubu no mu myaka iri imbere, bashobora kurwara indwara nyinshi zijanye no guhema, kansere, kwononekara kw'ingingo z'umubiri, hamwe no kwiyongera kw'abana bavukana ubumuga canke abavuka bapfuye.

Kubera ko ibigo vyose bitandatu vyo gutunganya amazi yanduye muri Gaza bitagikora, amazi yanduye ataratunganywa ubu arivanga n'amazi ari munsi y'ubutaka canke akinjira mu kiyaga Mediterane.

Ibintu biherutse kwunyurwa n'imvura nyinshi yaguye mu gihe c'imbeho. Iyo mvura yatumye amazi y'imvura avangana n'amazi yanduye, mu nyuma aca mu mabarabara no mu bibanza birimwo amahema acumbitsemwo abantu bahunze.

Kenshi gupima ubwoko n'urugero rw'ibihumanya ibidukikije ntigushoboka, kuko amalaboratware yo muri Gaza yasambuwe. Vyongeye, Israel irashiraho inzitizi mu bijanye no kwinjiza ibikoresho vyihariye vyo gupima hamwe n'abahinga.

BBC yarasavye igisirikare ca Israel kugira ico kivuga kuri ivyo.

Ishami rya ONU rijejwe ibidukikije (UNEP) ryavuze ko impungenge z'umutekano na zo zabujije abahinga baryo kuja muri Gaza mu bihe vyahera.

Mu cegeranyo cayo, Oxfam isaba ko hakorwa isuzuma ryuzuye kandi ryigenga ry'ibidukikije muri Gaza, kugira ngo hamenyekane ahari ingorane ziterwa n'ibintu bihumanya imbere y'uko igikorwa co gukuraho ibisigarira gitangura. Ivuga kandi ko hakwiye kwitwararikwa cane umutekano w'abakozi bazokora ico gikorwa.

Ambasade ya Israel yaneguye cane ico cegeranyo, ivuga ko cisunze amafoto yafashwe n'ibigendajuru "hamwe n'ivyiyumviro bitagenzuwe, kandi uburyo cakozwemwo ntibwubahiriza amategeko y'ubuhinga n'ubushakashatsi bwimbitse kandi bukenewe kugira icigwa gisuzumwe bikwiye".

Ivuga ko ivyo ico cegeranyo cashitseko ku bijanye n'ubutaka hamwe n'amazi ari munsi y'ubutaka muri Gaza, kitafatiye ku mihora yo mu kuzimu y'ibirometero amajana icibwa na Hamas. Ivyo, nk'uko Israel ibivuga, bituma ico cegeranyo kibamwo amakosa akomeye kuva ku ntango.

Abaganga bo muri Gaza basanzwe bavuga ko indwara zijanye no guhema zirushiriza kwiyongera. Izo ndwara ziterwa n'umukungugu hamwe n'umwanda uva mu nyubakwa zasambuwe, no ku bantu bahunze baturira ubumwanya, impuzu zishaje n'ibipuguru kugira ngo bashobore kwota no guteka.

Indwara zifatira mu mara zifitaniye isano n'amazi mabi hamwe n'isuku rike.

Dr Alaa Abu Hajar, umuganga w'indwara z'urukoba w'Umunya Palestina, yabwiye BBC ko kuva intambara itanguye, yabonye ko indwara z'urukoba zidakira ziyongereye incuro zitanu. Avuga ati: "Hari imbeba, imicafu n'amazi mabi bikwiragiye mu mabarabara. Ikibabaje, abana ni bo bagirwako ingaruka cane."

Abarimyi hamwe n'abarovyi bavuga ko uguhumana kw'ubutaka n'ikiyaga bituma badashobora kuronsa abantu ivyo kurya bitekanye.

Yidoga, umurovyi Abu al-Abed Sultan yagize ati: "Amazi yanduye ava mu mazu n'ayo mu bisagara asukwa mu kiyaga atabanje gutunganywa, kandi ivyo ni ivyago bikomeye."

Abandanya ati: "Hari kandi ibisigarira vy'amazu vyisuka mu kiyaga. Iyo tumanuye insenga ni vyo dufata hamwe n'imicafu. Ivyo vyonona ibidukikije vyo mu kiyaga. Biragira n'ingaruka ku mafi, na twebwe zikadushikira."

Kuva intambara itangura muri Gaza, Abanyapalestina nibura 74.746 barishwe, nk'uko bivugwa n'ubushikiranganji bw'amagara bugenzurwa na Hamas, ibitigiri ONU ivuga ko vyizewe. ONU ivuga kandi ko ubuzima bw'abanyagihugu hafatiwe ku vyo bakeneye bukibandanya kuba bubi cane.

Israel yashimangiye ko kwubaka Gaza ku rugero runini bizoshoboka ari uko Hamas n'iyindi mihari y'Abanyapalestina irwana bashize hasi ibirwanisho bose.
